POLITICAL PRZSONERS IN WARD ROAD GAOL ASK FOR 
~ RELEASE _TO SERVE COUNTRY 


During the past few years, the various Police 
Stations of the International Settlement arrested many 
political prisoners who were sentenced to various terms 
of imprisonment by the Second Branch of the Kiangsu High 
Court, and who are now being held in the Ward Road Gaol. 

After the outbreak of local hostilities, 
these political prisoners, who decided that the time had 
come for them to serve their country, sent a joint petition 
to the authorities asking fer the restoration of their 
liberty in order to enable them to offer themselves for 
the service of the country. 

It is learned that the authorities are in 
agreement in prinoiple with the request of the political 
prisoners, but the procedure to be used will require 
discussion. The release of the political prisoners may 
probably materialize within a short period.

November 10, 1937. Morning Translation.

Eastern District have been removed by Japanese troops
and transported to Japan.
According to information received from
reliable sources, several thousand tons of steel bars
valued at several million dollars, stored in the various
warehouses of the Tsai Zung Mou Metal Shop (蔡仁茂) in
Hongkew, have been removed.
The warehouses on Kwenming, Liaoyang, Tongshan,
Point and Dalny Roads have also been completely looted and
the premises are being occupied by large numbers of
Japanese troops.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers:

RELEASE OF CONVICTED PRISONERS

After the outbreak of the local Sino-
Japanese hostilities, the Nantao District Court released
about 600 prisoners detained in the detention house.
During the past three months, about 600 new
criminals were arrested by the Police Bureau. On
November 8 and 9, the Nantao District Court set free
300 prisoners convicted of minor offences. It is learned
that, if necessary, more such prisoners will be released
later on.

1937年11月10日。晨间译件。

东区已被日军撤走并运往日本。
据可靠消息来源称，存放在虹口蔡仁茂五金号（Tsai Zung Mou Metal Shop）各仓库内的价值数百万美元的数千吨钢筋已被运走。
昆明路、辽阳路、唐山路、Point路（原文不清，疑为某路名）及大连路上的仓库也已被彻底洗劫，大量日军正占据这些场所。

《立报》及其他本地报纸：

释放已决犯

当地中日战事爆发后，南市区法院释放了拘押在拘留所中的约600名囚犯。在过去三个月中，警察局逮捕了约600名新罪犯。11月8日和9日，南市区法院释放了300名因轻罪被判刑的囚犯。据悉，如有必要，日后还将释放更多此类囚犯。

October 20, 1937.    4    Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers (Nanking Telegram) :-

CONVICTS FOR MILITARY SERVICE

As the employment of convicts for military
service during war time will relieve the congestion in the
gaols and diminish the dangers from air raids by enemy
planes, and moreover as such work will be of some assistance
to the military authorities, the Ministry of Justice on
October 18 issued a circular order to the various provincial
High Courts instructing them to order all gaols to carry
out this scheme and to submit reports as soon as possible.

1937年10月20日。 4 晨间译件。

《申报》及其他本地报纸（南京电）：

征召囚犯服兵役

由于在战时征用囚犯服兵役可以缓解监狱拥挤状况，减少敌机空袭造成的危险，而且此类工作对军事当局也有所助益，司法部于10月18日发布通令，指示各省高等法院命令所有监狱执行此方案，并尽快提交报告。

Further to my report dated Sept. 27, 1937,
on the subject of the release of prisoners, Mr. Chen Tih Ming
of the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau telephoned this
morning stating that the Shanghai City District Court has
just received a communication from the Ministry of Justice,
Nanking, conveying instructions to liberate prisoners serving
sentences of less than five years on criminal offences.
Mr. Chen adds that the Shanghai 1st Special District Court
(Inter. Settlement) may have received a similar despatch from
Nanking.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No............
S.2 Special Branch    XXXXXX
REPORT    Date, Sept. 27 1937.
Subject (in full)....Reported instructions from Ministry of Justice to release
prisoners in criminal cases serving imprisonment less than 5 years.
Made by........ and.................... Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

Enquiries made from the local Tangpu, the Chinese
Court in the City and the S.C.G.Police Bureau show that they
have not received an official despatch or instructions from
Nanking Ministry of Justice re the release of prisoners
serving imprisonment less than five years in criminal cases.
The only information is from the press. They promise to
communicate with the S.M.P. as soon as instructions to this
effect are received.
The Chinese Authorities are worried as to how
the prisoners can be disposed of if the order apply to
release of the convicts in Shanghai.
I suggest that the Municipal Advocate approach
the First Special District Court for information.

（批：DBR. 27/9.）

Tan Shao Liang
Superintendent.

D. C. (Cr. & Sp. Branches).

经向本地塘浦、上海市中国法院及上海市警察局查询，显示他们尚未收到南京司法部关于释放刑事案件中刑期不满五年囚犯的正式公文或指令。目前唯一的信息来源是报刊。他们承诺一旦收到此类指令，将立即与上海公共租界工部局警务处联系。
中国当局担心，如果该命令适用于释放上海的已决犯，该如何处置这些囚犯。
我建议由市政律师向第一特区地方法院查询信息。

Lih Pao publishes the following telegram from Nanking :-

MINISTRY OF JUSTICE ORDERS RELEASE OF PRISONERS
SERVING LESS THAN FIVE YEARS

The Ministry of Justice has issued a circular
order to the various grades of Courts throughout the
country to the effect that during the period of the war
of resistance all criminal offenders whose cases have been
concluded and who have been sentenced to terms of imprison-
ment for less than five years shall be liberated.

司法部命令释放刑期不满五年的囚犯

recently released from Soochow Military Gaol, who stated that
he had been informed by a political prisoner detained in Ward Road
Gaol. (The method of communication was not stated and the
whereabouts of Pan Pau Min is not known). Chief Inspector
White, attached to the Judicial Police, was communicated with
and stated that such an appeal should as a matter of routine
be forwarded through his office, but no such appeal came to
his notice. Mr. Grant, Governor of Ward Road Gaol, when
communicated with, stated that an appeal, dated 13-8-37, had
been made by political prisoners in Ward Road Gaol, requesting
their release in order to serve their country, or failing their
release, that pay earned by them whilst detained in Gaol, should
be donated to the Government as war funds. The appeal was not
forwarded by order of Capt. Wahl, at that time i/c of the Gaol.

Sin Wan Pao 20

POLITICAL PRISONERS IN WARD ROAD GAOL ASK FOR
RELEASE TO SERVE COUNTRY

During the past few years, the various Police
Stations of the International Settlement arrested many
political prisoners who were sentenced to various terms
of imprisonment by the Second Branch of the Kiangsu High
Court, and who are now being held in the Ward Road Gaol.
After the outbreak of local hostilities,
these political prisoners, who decided that the time had
come for them to serve their country, sent a joint petition
to the authorities asking for the restoration of their
liberty in order to enable them to offer themselves for
the service of the country.
It is learned that the authorities are in
agreement in principle with the request of the political
prisoners, but the procedure to be used will require
discussion. The release of the political prisoners may
probably materialize within a short period.

（批：C 考）
（批：wz 2/19.）
pages.zh:
《新闻报》 20

提篮桥监狱政治犯请求释放报效国家

过去几年间，公共租界各捕房逮捕了许多政治犯，这些人被江苏高等法院第二分院判处不同期限的监禁，目前正关押在提篮桥监狱。
当地战事爆发后，这些政治犯认为报效国家的时机已到，遂联名向当局请愿，要求恢复自由，以便投身报国。
据悉，当局原则上同意政治犯的请求，但具体执行程序尚需讨论。政治犯的释放可能在短期内实现。

（批注：C 考）
（批注：wz 2/19.）

September 23, 1937.
Afternoon Translation

Lih Pao publishes the following telegram from Nanking :-

MINISTRY OF JUSTICE ORDERS RELEASE OF PRISONERS
SERVING LESS THAN FIVE YEARS

The Ministry of Justice has issued a circular
order to the various grades of Courts throughout the
country to the effect that during the period of the war
of resistance all criminal offenders whose cases have been
concluded and who have been sentenced to terms of imprison-
ment for less than five years shall be liberated.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers :-

ENEMY FORCES SUFFER REVERSE AT LIUHANG SECTOR

Heavy fighting took place at Liuhang yesterday.
At about 2 p.m. a detachment of enemy forces launched a
severe attack on the Chinese positions at Mang Wei ( 孟湾 )
in the vicinity of Liuhang. As soon as the enemy vanguards
had approached within a reasonable distance, the Chinese
defenders made a surprise counter-attack and completely
routed the invaders who took to flight, leaving about 50
prisoners and 30 others killed.
At about 5 p.m. another fierce engagement
took place between the Chinese troops and the enemy forces
entrenched to the north of Miaohang along the Wontsaopeng
Creek. At about 4 p.m. an enemy transport company, whilst
escorting a number of cases of ammunition, entered the
Chinese lines by mistake and was immediately surrounded
with the result that six enemy soldiers were taken captive
while 12 cases of rifle ammunition were seized.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

MEETING OF ASSOCIATION OF CHINESE RETURNED STUDENTS
FROM JAPAN

The Association of Chinese Returned Students
from Japan held a meeting yesterday. Mr. Yuan Chi ( 袁琦 )
presided. The following resolutions were passed :-
1) That speeches in the Japanese language be made through
broadcasting stations and that pamphlets in the Japanese
language be distributed in order to arouse the feelings
of the Japanese.
2) That a conversazione about war affairs be held.
3) That Chinese returned students from Japan having
special ability be collected in order to enable them
to render service to the nation.
4) That solicitation of members be continued.
At the meeting, Messrs Faung I ( 方治 ),
Lei Tseng ( 雷震 ), Kuo Mei-shu ( 郭沫若 ) and 12 others
were appointed standing members.

1937年9月23日。
午后译件

《立报》刊登如下南京电文：

司法部命令释放刑期不满五年的囚犯

司法部已向全国各级法院发布通令，大意是在抗战期间，所有案件已审结并被判处不满五年徒刑的刑事罪犯应予释放。

《立报》及其他本地报纸：

敌军在浏河地段受挫

昨日浏河发生激战。下午2时许，一股敌军对浏河附近孟湾的中国阵地发动猛烈攻击。当敌军先锋接近至有效距离时，中国守军发动突袭反击，彻底击溃入侵者，敌军溃逃，留下约50名俘虏及30具尸体。
下午5时许，中国军队与沿蕴藻浜（Wontsaopeng Creek）在庙行以北构筑工事的敌军之间再次爆发激烈战斗。下午4时许，一支敌军运输连在护送一批弹药箱时误入中国防线，随即被包围，结果6名敌军士兵被俘，12箱步枪弹药被缴获。

《大公报》及其他本地报纸：

留日同学会会议

留日同学会昨日举行会议。袁琦先生主持。通过以下决议：
1) 通过广播电台发表日语演讲，并发放日语宣传册，以唤起日本人的情感。
2) 举行关于战事的座谈会。
3) 集结有特殊才能的留日归国学生，以便为国家服务。
4) 继续招募会员。
会上，方治、雷震、郭沫若等12人被任命为常务委员。

SHANGHAI TIMES - 24.9.37.
25/3J

Short Term Convicts
To Be Released

Prisoners who have been
sentenced to, or are serving,
imprisonment terms not longer
than five years have been
ordered released from peniten-
tiaries throughout the country
by the Ministry of Justice,
according to a Nanking special
despatch to the "Lih Pao" in
its issue yesterday morning.
The wholesale release was
reportedly grounded on the
defensive war China is now
fighting against Japan and the
fact that all man power avail-
able should be mobilized for
the struggle.—Central News.

25/3J

短期囚犯
将被释放

据昨晨《立报》刊登的南京专电称，司法部已命令全国各地的感化院释放已被判处或正在服刑且刑期不超过五年的囚犯。

September 8, 1937.
Afternoon Translation.

Ta Kung Pao (comment) :-

JAPAN'S REPLY TO THE BRITISH NOTE

In connection with the shooting of Sir Hughe
Knatchbull-Hugessen, the British Ambassador to China,
by Japanese aeroplanes, the Japanese Government on
September 7 sent a reply to the British note of protest.
This reply is worthless for the Japanese Government
attempts to evade the responsibility by saying that
investigations into the affair have not yet been completed
and that it does not admit that the affair was committed
by Japanese aeroplanes. In the Diet, the Japanese
Government eventually declared that the point referred
to in the British note that Japanese planes should not
attack non-combatants constituted an insult to the
Imperial Navy.
A nation should protect its prestige. The
mild nature of the British note to Japan makes one
understand her characteristic of a great nation. What
can one feel towards the cunning attitude of Japan?

Ta Kung Pao (Evening Edition) :-

ARRIVAL IN SHANGHAI OF PRISONERS RELEASED FROM THE
KIANGSU PENITENTIARY, SOOCHOW

Of the total number of offenders released
recently from the Kiangsu Penitentiary at Soochow, more
than 50 have arrived in Shanghai. At first they were
accommodated at the Shanghai Foreign Firms Chinese Staff
Club, Foochow Road. At present they are staying on the
premises of the Hwa Yung Middle School (華光中學), Yu
Yuen Road. They are at present awaiting work to be
assigned to them by the Shanghai Enemy-Resisting Support
Association, which they had approached upon their arrival.
The Shanghai Cultural Circles' National
Salvation Aversion Association has already collected
several hundred dollars contributions towards the maintenance
of their livelihood.

（印：BRITISH COMMISSIONER FOR FOREIGN AFFAIRS (GRAND BRANCH) SEP 1937）

《大公报》（评论）：-

日本对英国照会的答复

针对日本飞机射击英国驻华大使许阁森爵士（Sir Hughe Knatchbull-Hugessen）一事，日本政府于9月7日就英国的抗议照会发出答复。该答复毫无价值，因为日本政府试图以调查尚未完成为由推卸责任，并否认此事系日本飞机所为。在议会中，日本政府最终宣称，英国照会中提及的日本飞机不应攻击非战斗人员一点，构成了对帝国海军的侮辱。
一个国家应当维护其威望。英国致日本照会的温和性质让人理解其作为大国的特质。对于日本这种狡诈的态度，人们作何感想？

《大公报》（晚刊）：- 1937年9月8日 (下午)

从苏州江苏监狱获释的囚犯抵达上海

近期从苏州江苏监狱获释的罪犯总数中，已有五十余人抵达上海。起初他们被安置在福州路的上海外商华员俱乐部。目前他们居住在愚园路华文中學（華文中學）校内。他们目前正在等待上海抗敌后援会分配工作，该会在他们抵达时曾与其接洽。
上海文化界救亡协会已募集数百元捐款，用于维持他们的生活。

C. O. S. 收
C 9月10日
